chunks: And from him, from Safwan, from al-Ala' and Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, all of them, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (Imams), upon them be peace, who said:

I asked him about a man who left a slave among a group of people, and one of them testified that the deceased had freed him. He said: 'If the witness is reliable, he is not liable (for compensation), and his testimony is accepted, and the slave is given time to pay the value, and whatever remains belongs to the heirs.'

key_terms.اسْتُسْعِيَ: He was given time to pay

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one person testifies that their master freed them before death?
ai.summary: This narration from Sahih al-Tusi details the procedure for 'itq bi-l-mal' (manumission by payment) when a slave's status is contested among multiple heirs. It establishes that a single reliable witness can validate the owner's intent to free the slave, triggering a period for the slave to pay the agreed value to the heirs, with any surplus retained by them. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the validity of individual testimony in manumission cases, balancing the rights of heirs with the slave's path to freedom.
